events.title: SOAR Into Strategy: A Strengths-Based Approach to Strategic Planning
events.description: Already thinking about next year? Come figure it out with SOAR, a strengths-based approach that starts with what your business does best. Strategic planning doesn’t have to begin with what’s wrong. What might become possible if your next strategic conversation started by discovering what your organization does exceptionally well—and then used those strengths to explore opportunities, imagine the future, and define meaningful results? In this highly interactive five-hour workshop, participants will experience SOAR—Strengths, Opportunities, Aspirations and Results , a strengths-based approach to strategic thinking grounded in Appreciative Inquiry. Rather than simply learning another planning framework, you’ll experience SOAR from three perspectives: yourself, your organization, and the people whose voices can help shape its future. Through individual reflection, appreciative interviews, partner conversations, and practical strategic planning exercises, you’ll explore what gives your organization life at its best, identify emerging possibilities, clarify aspirations for the future, and consider the results that would demonstrate meaningful success. You’ll also explore an important question for today’s leaders: What changes when strategy is created with people rather than simply presented to them? As organizations begin preparing for their upcoming strategic planning cycles, this workshop offers a practical way to create richer strategic conversations, engage stakeholders, and build greater ownership in turning ideas into action. During the workshop, you will: Experience SOAR personally before applying it organizationally Learn how Appreciative Inquiry can strengthen strategic conversations Practice conducting an appreciative organizational interview Develop a preliminary SOAR for your own organization Identify emerging strategic priorities and possibilities Consider whose voices need to be included in strategic planning Design a SOAR conversation you can take back to your organization You’ll leave with practical questions, tools, and a process you can immediately use to begin a different kind of strategic conversation. Who should attend? Business owners, executives, HR and organizational-development professionals, nonprofit leaders, managers, consultants, entrepreneurs, strategic-planning facilitators, and anyone responsible for helping an organization determine where it wants to go next. Come prepared to think differently about strategy—and leave prepared to start a conversation that can move your organization forward.

events.title: It’s Not You, It’s Your Lead Magnet, a 20Fathoms Breakfast Lab
events.description: This Week at Breakfast Lab You’ve run the cold email campaigns. You’ve tried the paid ads. You’ve posted the content. But sales still aren’t where you expected—and week after week, you’re stuck guessing where your next customer is going to come from. Here’s the real problem: most marketing today is robotic. It all looks the same, and none of it gives a lead a reason to stick around. Join Blake Grewal of The Lead Magnet Company to learn how to build lead magnets that create an immediate “aha” moment. The kind of moment that pulls in more leads and makes it a no-brainer for them to become customers. In this session, we’ll cover: Lead Magnet Showcase — a look at the different types of lead magnets available to you The AHA Moment Framework — how to build magnets that improve marketing performance and shorten your sales cycle Right Place, Right Time — how to get your magnet in front of the right customer at the right moment Bonus: every attendee gets access to the Lead Magnet Secrets Bundle for immediate support building their next lead magnet You’ll walk away with: The exact type of lead magnet your business should be offering A live grade on your current lead magnet(s) About the Presenter Blake Grewal is the founder of The Lead Magnet Company, where he helps B2B tech and service companies turn cold traffic into leads that actually convert. He shares daily lead magnet tips and is behind the upcoming Lead Magnet Lab, a new Skool community launching this October. Blake’s path into lead generation came through growth: he’s held growth and partnerships roles at startups including Codelist and ModernTax, and has spent the past several years helping founders build the systems that carry a lead all the way to a sale. About Breakfast Lab Breakfast Lab is a weekly event at 20Fathoms where you’ll get expert guidance to help meet your most pressing startup needs. Connecting you to the right tools and the right people at the right time. These events are held in person and offered virtually. There is no cost to attend. Coffee and a light breakfast are provided. Walk-ins are welcome. And if you’d like to stay and keep working, coworking at 20Fathoms is free on Thursdays for Breakfast Lab attendees.

events.title: Women in Tech Meetup – Traverse City
events.description: Join us for connection, empowerment, and lots of fun! Each month Women in Tech gathers to build community and support amongst women working in, or interested in, the tech industry and tech-related roles. This meetup is casual, fun, and easy to drop into. We talk about what we’re currently working on, share our stories, and pool our collected expertise to support each other on our journeys. This informal meetup is meant to help women build local connections and work on their professional growth (yeah, support systems!). Gatherings are often made up of half-returning and half-new women, creating a welcoming and approachable energy. This event is free and open to all, including students! Light snacks will be provided. Registration is requested to ensure ample seating, but walk-ins are always welcome. Look for the Women in Tech/20Fathoms signage. We can’t wait to see you! About 20Fathoms Based in Traverse City, 20Fathoms is a nonprofit organization and the hub for entrepreneurship and innovation in Northwest Michigan. The 20Fathoms team works with entrepreneurs of all stages and industries, and also offers specialized services to meet the unique needs of technology-focused startups. Programs include startup education, business coaching, TCNewTech pitch competitions, access to capital, a vibrant coworking space, and general resources and support. For more information visit: https://20fathoms.org/ Thank you to our event partner Earthen Ales

They’ll walk through their progress, demonstrate what they’ve made, and share what’s next. Investors will get an up-close look at the emerging Great Lakes water-tech companies on the rise. Mentors and ecosystem partners will see what their time and resources helped build. The Traverse City community will get a front-row seat to the founders helping shape the future of freshwater and BlueTech innovation right here in Northern Michigan. Live showcases, working tech, and the people behind the future of Great Lakes water tech. Drinks and food on us. Register for Event

events.title: Build Guild : Traverse City @ Earthen Ales
events.description: Build Guild Traverse City We’re a fun, friendly gathering for web people of all sorts — developers, designers, producers, friends of people whose nephew makes websites on weekends. We’ll probably be a bit geeky, we want you to be too. All are welcome to Build Guild. Some attendees bring their significant others from time to time, and we’ve even seen a couple kids (if your venue allows it). We just want people that want to be there. There are no talks, no presentations, and no topics forced upon people to discuss. People show up, they grab a drinks if they want one, find a hand to shake are start chatting. Build Guild is a low-to-no-pressure environment. People do network with one another at Build Guilds, but it’s not your typical networking event. It’s low-key, laid-back, and much more focused on sharing stories over a beer than a business-card free-for-all. We’ve had the occasional pushy recruiter show up here and there, but ten minutes and a beer later, they’re laid back just like everyone else. Build Guild provides the least amount of structure needed to get people regularly chatting with one another face-to-face.
